evaluations.label: A
errors: "Target group 15-35 years" presented as a decision; the transcript shows the target group was left open (under 65 floated, then objectives preferred over an age group)
Action item "Investigate technical feasibility for rechargeable battery" was never assigned; the User Interface Designer only mused about whether a battery is needed at all
Action item "Provide updated market research data" is listed as unassigned, though the Marketing Expert said she would email more age numbers if she got them
"Chip converts energy to data" is a loose paraphrase; the Industrial Designer described the chip converting electrical energy into data, acceptable but compressed
strengths: Captures key market research numbers (75%, 80%, 10%, over 50% lose remotes)
Lists the four working-design components and the agreed functions (large buttons, hidden extras, loss prevention)
Includes the 12.5 euro production cost limit
weaknesses: Very terse fragments; hard for an absent reader to follow the reasoning
States an unsettled target group as decided
Misses the real action items: questionnaire and summary, individual work assignments, PM posting minutes and slides, coach emails
Omits the 25 euro retail price and the sliding-panel idea

evaluations.label: B
errors: Next step says "Working design presentation not yet on the server; save from email into shared folder"; in the transcript the Industrial Designer had already uploaded the working design presentation, and it was the Project Manager's presentation that was missing from the server
"age segmentation less useful than lifestyle/attitude targeting"; the alternative discussed was spending power/income and TV ownership, not lifestyle or attitude
"Target group: broad appeal, roughly under 65" reads as settled, while the group explicitly found it hard to narrow and left it open
strengths: Rich and well-organized coverage of research findings, including RSI, 65% channel zapping, and voice recognition by age
Clear list of agreed functions (locator, large buttons, hidden secondary functions, battery, brand aesthetic)
Includes both price points (25 euro retail, 12.50 production), scope (TV only, no teletext) and brand colors
Captures post-meeting tasks: questionnaire, summary, individual workstreams, coach emails, possible extra age data
weaknesses: One next step misidentifies which presentation was missing from the shared folder
Does not assign owners to most next steps; misses the PM's commitment to post minutes and slides
Slight overstatement that the target group was resolved

evaluations.label: C
errors: Attributes "potential LCD screens or sliding hatches" to the technical-interface presenter's talk; the LCD screen came from the Marketing Expert's research and the sliding hatch came up later in group discussion
"Management decided against including teletext support or voice recognition"; management decided teletext only, voice recognition was set aside by the team
Unresolved question "Would adding a 'find my remote' beep function fit within budget?" was never raised, and contradicts its own outline stating the locator was an agreed function
"Action Items: (none)" is wrong; the PM assigned the questionnaire and summary, individual work (components concept, UI concept, market trend watching) and committed to posting minutes and slides
"improve convenience and location tracking" overstates the cradle idea, which was only said to help keep the remote in one place
strengths: Reasonably complete outline of the agenda, three presentations, new requirements and agreed functions
Includes both price points and the 12:13 start with a 40-minute meeting
Notes the target group debate between 15-35 and a broader range
weaknesses: Generic speaker numbers make it hard to know who said what
Invented unresolved questions and some misattributions

evaluations.label: D
errors: Minor: the sidebar of individual work says "Each area had a corresponding concept or work focus", which is vague but not wrong; no substantive factual errors found
strengths: Correctly states that the target demographic was left open, with the range of suggestions (15-35, under 65, 20-55) and the spending-ability alternative
Accurate on scope (TV only, no teletext because of the internet), 25 euro separate sale, 12.50 production ceiling, brand colors and slogan
Captures the agreed functions, sliding panel idea, chip-transmission caveat, cradle idea and living-room space note
Correctly identifies that the PM's own presentation was missing from the server and that the PM will post minutes and slides
Timestamps for each point help verification
weaknesses: Action items list only the PM's tasks; team questionnaire, summary and individual work are in the body but not in the action list
Omits the Marketing Expert's offer to email more age data before the next meeting
Some RSI and channel-zapping detail is compressed

rationale: D is the most accurate and correctly represents what was decided versus left open (notably the unsettled target group) and the file follow-ups, with timestamps. B is the most detailed and very useful, but misidentifies which presentation was missing from the shared folder and overstates the target group as settled. C covers the meeting broadly but has misattributions, invents unresolved questions that contradict its own outline, and lists no action items. A is terse, states the 15-35 target group as decided, invents unassigned action items, and misses the actual assignments.
